subject: design-studies
title: Ergonomic Dimensions: Fit the Chair and Desk to the Student

slides.heading: Ergonomic Dimensions: Fit the Chair and Desk to the Student
bullets: How one chair-and-desk set is sized from one student: the lower-leg height sets the seat height, the hip breadth plus clearance sets the seat width, and the seated elbow height sets the desk height - with a fit bar that climbs as each fit gap closes
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we size one chair and one desk for one student, starting from the student measurements and letting each measurement set one dimension.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Explain how ergonomic dimensions are set from the user measurements: seat height from lower-leg height, seat width from hip breadth plus clearance, desk height from seat height plus seated elbow height
Work the numbers for one student: lower leg 40 cm, hip breadth 36 cm, seated elbow 24 cm above the seat
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to size a chair and desk for any student from three measurements.

slides.heading: One standard size for every student - does it fit anyone?
bullets: A chair built to average measurements can be sat on by almost everyone
But sitting on a chair is not the same as the chair fitting: feet dangle and desks sit too high
slides.notes: Ask the class: if a chair is built to the average size, who does it actually fit? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the animation sizes the chair from one student instead.

slides.heading: Ergonomic design sizes the product from the user
bullets: Each dimension of the product is set from a measurement of the user, not from an average of many users
Seat height equals lower-leg height, seat width equals hip breadth plus clearance, desk height equals seat height plus seated elbow height
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: measure the user first, then let each measurement set one dimension - the average never enters the design.

slides.heading: Measure the student: lower leg, hips and seated elbow
bullets: The student is measured before anything is built: lower-leg height 40 cm, hip breadth 36 cm, seated elbow 24 cm above the seat
The fit bar starts empty because no dimension has been set yet
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the three measurements and the empty fit bar: these three numbers will set the whole chair and desk.

slides.heading: Set the seat height: it rises to the lower-leg height
bullets: The seat rises until its height equals the lower-leg height of 40 cm
The feet rest flat on the floor, the gap under the thigh closes, and the fit bar climbs to one third
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and follow the seat rising: the gap closes exactly when the seat height reaches the lower-leg height.

slides.heading: Set the seat width and the desk height from the body
bullets: The seat widens to the hip breadth plus clearance: 36 + 4 = 40 cm
The desk top settles at seat height plus seated elbow height: 40 + 24 = 64 cm, so the forearms rest level, and the fit bar climbs to two thirds
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and work both sums aloud: width from the hips plus clearance, desk height from the seat plus the elbow height.

slides.heading: Wrong turn: one standard size leaves feet dangling
bullets: A standard chair built to average measurements leaves this student feet dangling and the desk too high
The fitted sizes are restored - seat, width and desk each set from the student own measurements - and the fit bar fills
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and contrast the two fits: the standard size leaves every gap open, the measured sizes close them all and fill the fit bar.

slides.heading: Worked example: sizing the chair and desk from the measurements
bullets: Seat height = lower-leg height = 40 cm; seat width = hip breadth + clearance = 36 + 4 = 40 cm
Desk height = seat height + seated elbow height = 40 + 24 = 64 cm
slides.notes: Work it slowly: measurement one sets the seat height, measurement two plus clearance sets the width, and the desk height is built up from the seat. At each step ask: which measurement set this dimension?

slides.heading: Your turn: size a chair for a new student
bullets: In pairs: a new student has lower-leg height 38 cm, hip breadth 34 cm and seated elbow height 23 cm - set the seat height, the seat width with 4 cm clearance, and the desk height
Then swap and check: did your partner set every dimension from a measurement, or slip back to a standard size?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for seat height 38 cm, seat width 38 cm, desk height 61 cm, then take two pairs answers.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says one standard size fits every user
Name the measurement that sets each dimension to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers tie every dimension to the measurement that sets it.
